gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Brushy single strokes, all one width, like a sign painter's afternoon. Origami grabs the eye with that unbroken line, while Noto Sans Lisu, a plain sans, keeps its wide s curves and tight ascenders quietly doing the reading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-saira: Hollow glass-tube letters with a brush-sign feel. Origami holds its tube thickness constant throughout, while Saira, a sans-serif, stretches its rounded letters tall and leaves a see-through gap in every s.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sarpanch: Cord-thick curves with a lowercase like poured lead. Sarpanch, a plain sans, has an open-mouthed e and compact ascenders, so paragraphs under Origami should read smoothly and approachably, with a contemporary ease.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sulphur-point: Poured-lead lowercase with a single-stroke brush swagger. What stands out is how Origami's brushy single stroke meets Sulphur Point, a sans with marker-like weight, bulky lowercase and gaps that stay open.
